clue.text: Front light flickering with unknown frequency

definitions.note: the clue's noun stands for an adjective naming how often something happens, here once every two weeks

indicators.note: a light that is flickering is unsteady and jumping about, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: Y is one of the algebraist's unknowns, alongside X and Z

explanation.surface: A headlamp starts to flicker at a rate nobody can measure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flickering' rearranges FRONTLIGHT into FORTNIGHTL, and the unknown Y finishes it. The clue's noun 'frequency' is loose for an adjective, but names the kind of word the answer is.
explanation.definitionFit: Once every two weeks is a rate of recurrence, which is what a frequency describes.

clue.text: Wonderful bit of imagination leading to one society founded by E Nesbit

definitions.note: names a group: the definition reads as the members of the society she helped found

parts.note: fab, short for fabulous, means wonderful

indicators.note: a bit of a word is here its first letter

parts.note: an means one

explanation.surface: A dash of wonderful imagination led to a club started by the children's author.
explanation.walkthrough: E Nesbit, author of The Railway Children, was a founding member of the Fabian Society, the British socialist group, in 1884.
explanation.definitionFit: The members of the gradualist socialist society co-founded by Nesbit take their name from it.

clue.text: Poet who's all right to like perhaps

parts.note: R stands for 'roger', all right, in radio signalling

indicators.note: perhaps marks the word as one possible arrangement of its letters

explanation.surface: A poet who happily agrees to be liked, maybe.
explanation.walkthrough: The radio operator's 'Roger', meaning all right, is shortened to its initial.
explanation.definitionFit: Rainer Maria Rilke wrote the Duino Elegies, among the best-known German-language poetry.

clue.text: Philosopher cooking schnitzel mostly before beginning to eat

indicators.note: cooking prepares and transforms the food, so the letters are mixed
mostly means all but the last letter
the beginning to a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A thinker is frying most of a veal escalope before starting his meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts SCHNITZEL to SCHNITZE, 'cooking' rearranges it to NIETZSCH, and 'beginning to' adds E from 'eat'.
explanation.definitionFit: The German author of Thus Spoke Zarathustra is one of modern philosophy's major figures.

clue.text: Chap we hear with a hypothesis formulated by Lovelock

indicators.note: we hear signals that a word is said aloud and spelt differently

parts.note: a guy is a chap

explanation.surface: Apparently a fellow came up with a scientific theory with James Lovelock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' makes GUY sound like GAI, then A follows.
explanation.definitionFit: James Lovelock's theory treats the Earth as a self-regulating whole, named after the Greek earth goddess.

clue.text: Actor at heart and an artist at dance

definitions.text: Actor at heart and an artist at dance

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its central letter

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
the volta is a lively Renaissance dance for couples

explanation.surface: A performer who is an actor at heart and a real artist when dancing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at heart' gives T, the middle of 'Actor'. The whole clue also describes John Travolta, film actor and the dancer of Saturday Night Fever.
explanation.definitionFit: John Travolta is a film star famous for his disco dancing in Saturday Night Fever.

clue.text: Shout wordlessly and cry endlessly about overdose

indicators.note: about means going round, so one piece surrounds the other
endlessly means the last letter is removed

parts.note: a yell is a cry

explanation.surface: Someone howls without words and sobs on and on over an overdose.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a crying fit; the yodeller's call is the wordless shout.
explanation.definitionFit: Alpine singing that switches between chest and falsetto voice is a wordless call.

clue.text: Regularly at a loss, without this? (, 1, )

indicators.note: taking letters at regular intervals means every other letter of the phrase is kept

explanation.surface: Would you be bewildered if you had no copy of this paper to hand?
explanation.walkthrough: Taking the second, fourth and sixth letters of ATALOSS gives the three initials. 'this' points to the paper the puzzle is printed in, the Times Literary Supplement; the bracketed commas are the page's odd enumeration.
explanation.definitionFit: The crossword appears in the Times Literary Supplement, so the clue's pointer to its own publication names that paper's initials.

clue.text: Cover of book by Du Maurier that's missing title's header

parts.note: Trilby is George du Maurier's 1894 novel

indicators.note: missing means lacking, so the letter is taken out

parts.note: the 's is 'is', a link; the word used is the pronoun

indicators.note: a word's header is its first letter

explanation.surface: The jacket of a Du Maurier novel has lost the first letter of its title.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing' takes T, the 'header' of 'title's', out of THAT, leaving HAT. Readers will think of Daphne du Maurier; it is her grandfather George.
explanation.definitionFit: A soft felt hat with an indented crown, named after the novel, is headwear and so a covering.

clue.text: Mowers getting badly chesty after start of spring

indicators.note: after places the first piece before what follows it in the answer
the start of a word is its first letter
done badly means messed up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Lawnmowers are giving people chest trouble at the beginning of spring.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests hay fever; the mowers are the old hand tools.
explanation.definitionFit: Long-bladed hand tools for cutting grass were the original mowing implements.

clue.text: Li'l Abner confused by introduction to Appalachian dancer

indicators.note: being confused means mixed up, so the letters of the cartoon name and the extra letter are scrambled
the introduction to a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: The hillbilly hero of the comic strip is baffled by a mountain dancer.
explanation.walkthrough: Li'l Abner is the hillbilly of Al Capp's American comic strip; 'by' only joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A ballet performer, especially a female one, is a kind of dancer.

clue.text: Miss Miller, said to be undone by Italy finally

indicators.note: something undone is untied and loosened, so the letters of the word are disarranged
finally points to the closing letter of the word

explanation.surface: Henry James's heroine is reported ruined at last by her Italian trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be undone' rearranges SAID into DAIS, and 'finally' adds the Y that ends 'Italy'. The surface is apt: Henry James's Daisy Miller dies of Roman fever in Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry James's novella title character is the American girl Daisy Miller.

clue.text: City of gold in Australia, Oz, receiving nearly nothing in return

parts.note: A is the international vehicle code for Austria but here stands for Australia, as in the abbreviation for the country

indicators.note: a return goes back the way it came, so the pieces are read backwards

parts.note: Oz, the familiar name for Australia, taken as written; receiving just means it is followed by the next piece

indicators.note: nearly means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: nothing is zero
the final circle-shaped letter of the word for nothing is the one dropped

explanation.surface: An Australian gold-rush town where the ounces come back to almost nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: The Australian gold-rush picture misleads: the city is in Tuscany, where 'in return' turns the whole of Oz plus almost-zero round.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tuscan city has long been a centre of goldsmithing and jewellery making.

clue.text: Under which Paterson's swagman sheltered, relaxed in the same place as raxiteles he'd originally chosen

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held: 'Under which Paterson's swagman sheltered, relaxed in the same place as raxiteles he'd originally chosen'. COOL + IB gives COOLIB, but AH cannot be had without leaving 'raxiteles' (likely the setter's name Praxiteles) and 'chosen' unaccounted for; the printed text looks garbled.
annotationWithheld.clue: Under which Paterson's swagman sheltered, relaxed in the same place as raxiteles he'd originally chosen

clue.text: Philosopher seen round about

indicators.note: turning a word round here means its letters are rearranged

parts.note: CA, short for circa, means about

explanation.surface: A thinker has been spotted roaming around.
explanation.walkthrough: CA is the abbreviation of Latin circa, 'about', familiar from dates.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman Stoic thinker and tutor to Nero is one of antiquity's best-known philosophers.

clue.text: "To that old village alehouse where / In -s is written 'Bear'" (John Betjeman)

definitions.text: "To that old village alehouse where / In -s is written 'Bear'" (John Betjeman)

parts.words: To that old village alehouse where / In -s is written 'Bear'
parts.note: a quotation from John Betjeman with a gap: the missing phrase is how the pub's sign is lit up

explanation.walkthrough: A fill-in-the-blank from Betjeman: the pub's name 'Bear' is spelt out in glowing gas-tube signs, the missing phrase with an S added.
explanation.definitionFit: Glowing gas-filled tubes are the usual material of lit-up pub and shop signs.

clue.text: Some Greek verses start to secure prizes I overlooked

indicators.note: the start to a word is its first letter
an item overlooked is left out, so the letter is dropped

parts.note: trophies are prizes
taken as written

explanation.surface: A student of Greek poetry begins to win awards, but is passed over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'start to' gives S from 'secure'; 'overlooked' drops I from TROPHIES, leaving TROPHES.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek choral odes the stanzas sung while the chorus turned were the units of verse.

clue.text: Old recluse exchanging two letters regarding a name

indicators.note: swapping a pair of letters in the word changes their places

parts.note: monastic means reclusive, like a monk

explanation.surface: An old hermit has swapped a couple of letters in his name.
explanation.walkthrough: Recluse is taken as an adjective here: living apart like monks.
explanation.definitionFit: The word derives from Greek onoma, so it describes things relating to names.

clue.text: Callers with energy for nothing; Miss Ashford's were young

indicators.note: one letter is put in place of another, signalled by putting it for the other

parts.note: visitors are callers
O looks like zero, nothing
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Guests bring vigour where there was none; Miss Ashford's were young.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' puts E in place of O in VISITORS. Daisy Ashford wrote The Young Visiters aged nine, misspelling and all.
explanation.definitionFit: Daisy Ashford's childhood novel is titled The Young Visiters, with its famous misspelling.

clue.text: One-time state of poems in new version of Hair

indicators.note: one piece goes in the middle of the other
a new version reworks the original, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: odes are lyric poems

explanation.surface: Lyrics have been added to a fresh production of the hippie musical.
explanation.walkthrough: Hair is the 1960s rock musical, which tempts a theatrical reading.
explanation.definitionFit: The former British colony in southern Africa is now Zimbabwe, so it is a country that no longer exists under that name.

clue.text: About to struggle with opponents which are seen in 1A,7A

parts.note: re means about or concerning
to vie is to strive or compete
West and South are opposing players at the bridge table

explanation.surface: About to fight it out with rivals over what the paper prints.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge, North-South play East-West, so W and S sit on opposite sides. 1A,7A is the fortnightly Times Literary Supplement, full of book critiques.
explanation.definitionFit: Critical appraisals of books are the staple content of the literary paper.

clue.text: American author with habitual response written in verse

parts.note: Edgar Allan Poe, the American writer of tales and poems
a tic is a habitual twitch or reflexive response

explanation.surface: An American writer has a reflexive habit of putting everything into rhyme.
explanation.definitionFit: Something composed in lines of verse is lyrical in form, in the manner of a poem.

clue.text: Instrument introducing Miss Holm, singing about being a millionaire

definitions.meaning: a keyboard instrument whose hammers strike metal plates, heard in the Sugar Plum Fairy dance

definitions.text: Miss Holm, singing about being a millionaire
definitions.meaning: the actress Holm sang 'Who Wants to Be a Millionaire?' with Sinatra in the film High Society

explanation.definitionFit: The bell-like keyboard instrument shares its name with the actress Holm of High Society.

clue.text: Abridged book about a popular Shakespearean mother

indicators.note: an abridged text is shortened, so the last letter goes

parts.note: a volume is a book

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the pair is read backwards

parts.note: in means popular or fashionable

explanation.surface: A shortened volume about a well-liked mother from the plays.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Abridged' cuts VOLUME to VOLUM; 'about' turns A + IN into NIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Coriolanus's formidable mother in Shakespeare's tragedy is a leading maternal role.

clue.text: Note returned unchanged

indicators.note: read backwards it is just the same, a word that reads alike both ways

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A memo comes back with no corrections at all.
explanation.walkthrough: The half-note reads the same backwards, which is the whole of the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A half-note lasting two crotchets is a musical note value.

clue.text: Author's cover modified slightly in the end

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', so the definition is the author alone

indicators.note: a slight change at the end shifts one letter near the close of the word to a new spot

parts.note: a mantle is a cloak, a cover

explanation.surface: A writer's dust jacket has been altered a little at the back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'modified slightly in the end' moves the L of MANTLE past the E. The author is Hilary Mantel, twice Booker winner for her Thomas Cromwell novels.
explanation.definitionFit: Hilary Mantel was the English novelist behind Wolf Hall, so the surname names a writer.

clue.text: Goodbye to Republican, one speaking a Turkic language

parts.note: ta-ta is a British informal way of saying goodbye

explanation.surface: Farewell to the Republican, someone who speaks a Central Asian tongue.
explanation.definitionFit: The Volga people of that name speak a language of the Turkic family.

clue.text: Couturier enveloped in Yazidi ornaments

indicators.note: enveloped in means wrapped inside the words, so the name is spelt across them

explanation.surface: A fashion designer is wrapped in the decorations of a Kurdish religious group.
explanation.walkthrough: The Yazidis are a Kurdish religious minority.
explanation.definitionFit: Christian Dior was a Paris fashion designer, which is what a couturier is.

clue.text: Collector of antiquities popular with El Greco initially

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: initially picks the opening letter of the painter's surname

parts.note: in means popular or fashionable

explanation.surface: An art collector is in favour, along with the work of a Spanish master.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' gives G from 'Greco'; EL is taken whole. Lord Elgin brought the Parthenon sculptures to Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: The seventh Earl of Elgin removed the Parthenon marbles to London, making him a notorious acquirer of ancient art.

clue.text: Blockbuster, American, about so called offensive philosopher

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the other pieces go round this one

parts.note: an epic is a big blockbuster film
US is short for American, from United States
the Tet Offensive of 1968 in the Vietnam War, so called after the lunar new year

explanation.surface: A big American film about the so-called offensive thinker.
explanation.walkthrough: Tet is the Vietnamese new year, which named the 1968 offensive in the Vietnam War.
explanation.definitionFit: The Stoic teacher of the first century, a freed slave, is a famous philosopher of antiquity.

clue.text: Egyptian God of storms put in his place

definitions.meaning: the Egyptian deity of chaos and storms, murderer of Osiris
placed or positioned, as of a thing laid down where it belongs

explanation.surface: The storm god of Egypt has been put firmly in his place.
explanation.definitionFit: Placing something in position is a common sense of the verb, and the storm deity of Egypt bears the same name.

clue.text: Monastic room, one with fancy decor by cheapskate

indicators.note: by means beside, so the miser comes next to the rest

parts.note: a miser is a cheapskate
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: fancy here is a verb-like signal that the letters are made elaborate, rearranged

explanation.surface: A room at a monastery fitted out with elaborate decoration by a skinflint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fancy' rearranges DECOR into CORDE; MISER comes beside I + CORDE.
explanation.definitionFit: In a monastery the misericord was a room where relaxed rules on diet applied.
